title: Staged Variant Sentinel: policy engine for progressive model switches with automatic containment
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a policy engine (Sentinel) that orchestrates staged model variant promotions, supports shadow/A-B arms, provides programmable step schedules (linear, anneal, fixed windows), and enforces guardrails with automatic rollback/quarantine behavior.
background: Teams frequently deploy new model variants and need deterministic, repeatable promotions that protect user-facing SLOs and output quality. Current ad-hoc scripts and manual checks lead to slow rollouts and occasional user impact. We need a platform-level policy engine tied to telemetry to automate safe promotions across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
goals: Provide a declarative policy schema for staged promotions (percent splits, duration per step, step-advance conditions)
Support shadow traffic collection and A/B arms with configurable metrics and divergence checks
Enforce guardrails (latency, error-rate, output-similarity, cost delta) with automatic rollback and quarantine rules
Expose runtime hooks for manual override, canary pinning, and forced rollback via Console/API
Produce per-step telemetry and an auditable event stream for compliance and postmortems
non_goals: Replacing full-featured experimentation platforms (we integrate, not replicate)
Model-level training or automated retraining decisions
Building a new low-latency inference path solely for canaries (use existing runtime paths)
proposed_design: Sentinel is a small stateful controller and policy evaluator. Users submit a StagedPromotion resource (via API/Console) that references a baseline variant and one or more candidate variants. A policy describes steps: percent routing, duration, gating metrics, and post-step actions (advance, pause, rollback, quarantine). The controller subscribes to per-route telemetry (latency, 5xx, p99, embeddings_similarity, token_cost) and computes step-level deltas. A scoring function aggregates metric deltas into a pass/fail decision using weighted thresholds. On fail, Sentinel can: 1) immediately cut traffic back to baseline, 2) move candidate to quarantine (no routing, but preserve logs), or 3) revert to previous step. For shadow arms, Sentinel mirrors requests to the candidate without routing real traffic and validates outputs using a configurable validator (embedding cosine with threshold or rule-based comparator). The policy schema is intentionally small and extensible; runtime enforces schema and rejects incompatible configs.
rollout_policy_dsl_example:
version: 1
name: staged-sentinel-demo
baseline: model:redwood-1.0
candidates:
  - id: r2
    model: model:redwood-1.1
    attributes: [quant-8bit]
steps:
  - id: step-0
    type: shadow
    duration: 30m
    actions:
      - collect: [latency_ms, err_rate, embed_cosine, token_cost]
  - id: step-1
    type: percent
    traffic: 1%
    duration: 15m
    gating:
      - metric: err_rate
        operator: lt
        threshold: 0.5%
      - metric: embed_cosine
        operator: gte
        threshold: 0.88
  - id: step-2
    type: anneal
    start: 1%
    end: 20%
    duration: 120m
    advance_on: "windowed-stable(5m)"
post_actions:
  on_fail: rollback_to: baseline
  quarantine: true
  notify: [slack:#inference-rollouts, pager:oncall]
guardrails_and_triggers: Latency regressions: p95 increase > 20% over baseline in a 5m sliding window triggers pause/fail
Error spike: 5xx rate > 0.75% absolute or > 3x baseline in a step window triggers immediate rollback
Output divergence: embedding cosine mean < configured threshold (default 0.85) for sampled requests triggers quarantine
Cost delta: per-token cost increase > 10% sustained for step duration marks policy as degraded and pauses progression
Manual override: operators can pin traffic or force rollback via API/Console; Sentinel must persist an audit event for the change
acceptance_criteria: Policy schema validator implemented and integrated into API (bad schema -> 422)
Controller can run a staged promotion end-to-end in a simulated environment (unit test harness)
Shadow step collects mirrored request/response pairs and computes embedding similarity within the pipeline
Auto-rollback triggers on defined guardrails and results in observable rollback events and alerting
Console shows per-step metrics, events, and provides a single-click rollback action
Backward-compatibility: existing simple percent traffic rules (legacy) accepted and translated to new schema
testing_plan: Unit: policy parser, validator, and scoring functions
Integration: end-to-end in staging with curated synthetic traffic (latency and error injection) and model stubs
Load: run multiple concurrent staged promotions to ensure controller scales and does not exceed control-plane QPS
Chaos: simulate metric stream delays and partial telemetry to validate conservative behavior (fail-closed)
Canary in Prod: small internal-only rollout to a feature-flagged workspace before general availability
telemetry_and_alerting: Per-step: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, token_cost, sample_delta_embed_cosine
Event stream: step_started, step_completed, step_failed, rollback_executed, manual_override
Alerts: step-failure-critical pager if rollback executed in production; step-pause-warning to Slack
Dashboard: per-promotion time-series with annotated step boundaries and traffic percentages
dependencies: Console: UI work for policy create/edit (PM/Design tickets)
open_questions: Default thresholds: should defaults be conservative (low false negatives) or permissive?
Metric windowing: what is the recommended sampling rate and window size for small-traffic canaries?
Quarantine lifecycle: how long do we retain quarantined variants and logs before auto-archiving?
Cost accounting: do we bill shadow traffic to customer usage or internal credits?
KPI weighting: how should teams specify relative importance of latency vs. fidelity?
notes: Design review scheduled 2025-02-18 with PM/Design/Runtime teams; sketch in drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/staged-sentinel (internal)
Proposed default guardrail set is intentionally conservative for first GA to reduce blast radius
Prefer a single code path in runtime for percent routing to avoid divergence between canary and baseline
We will reuse existing alerting channels and add a dedicated rollouts Slack channel for noisy but actionable alerts
